evidence.curator_note: Generic scheme R(+.)CR3 -> R. + (+)CR3: a saturated-alkane sigma C-C bond is ionized and dissociates, the charge going to the more-substituted carbon and the odd electron to the leaving alkyl radical. Instantiated by the curator as ETHANE (R = CR3 = CH3), the example the surrounding text discusses ('ionization of ethane increases the C-C bond length by ~30% and halves its bond dissociation energy'); by symmetry it gives CH3(+) + CH3(.). REPRESENTATION CAVEAT (honest): the saturated-alkane molecular ion is a sigma radical cation whose odd electron occupies the one-electron C-C bond and is NOT localizable on any single atom -- the book draws '+.' straddling the C-C bond, not on an atom. A CnH(2n+2) radical cation has no connected integer-bond Lewis/RDKit structure at all (37 valence electrons for ethane-> 6 two-electron bonds + 1 unpaired e-, i.e. one fewer bond than the 7 needed to connect 8 atoms), so the precursor mapped_smiles necessarily shows the NEUTRAL C-C skeleton (the real origin of the arrows) while the species charge=1/radical_electrons=1 fields record that it is the M+.. Book draws 0 curved arrows/fishhooks; the mechanism is denoted by the 'sigma' label over the reaction arrow. The two encoded moves are curator-supplied for a complete, balanced electron flow and map onto the book's own words: move <1> routes one electron of the C-C sigma bond to the leaving carbon (-> CH3.), move <2> routes the other sigma electron to EXTERNAL -- this IS the ionization the book states removes an electron 'from the saturated bond framework', leaving CH3(+). No arc is misrepresented as drawn.

rule_index cross-links equation 4.7 to IMS_4_7 ([C+.]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5 >> [C.]1.[C+]2[C]3[C]4[C]5) and to sigma_lowIE ([_A+.]1[I]2 >> [_A.]1.[I+]2). VERIFIED BOND-CHANGE MATCH: IMS_4_7 cleaves the C1-C2 sigma bond, sends atom1 [C+.] -> [C.] (the leaving neutral radical R.) and atom2 -> [C+] (the retained carbocation (+)CR3), which is exactly the book's R(+.)CR3 -> R. + (+)CR3. sigma_lowIE is the low-ionization-energy-heteroatom analogue (R-X, e.g. C-I) with the same topology _A(+.)-X -> _A. + X(+); it is a generalization, not a match for the all-carbon ethane case. MODEL-DIVERGENCE CAVEAT: both rules localize the '+.' on a carbon atom, which MOD's untyped graph model permits but RDKit rejects for a saturated alkane (the sibling explicit-H alkane rules IMS_4_3/IMS_4_8 place [C+.] on a 4-coordinate carbon, which RDKit refuses -- 'Explicit valence for atom C, 4, is greater than permitted'). The bond CHANGE the rules encode is faithful; only their atom-localized radical-cation precursor is not RDKit-representable, which is why this record's precursor mapped_smiles uses the neutral skeleton. All m/z values are curator-computed from the ethane instantiation.

The page prints no m/z and no relative intensity for this generic scheme; 15.0229 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of CH3(+) (electron-mass corrected) for the chosen ethane instantiation. Not a measurement.
